title: Chapter 89: Deep Well
html:
“Then what was your brother’s response?”

The man had already been unstable before the haunting. Chen Ge suspected that a threat would drive him to extremes, and what Fan Yu’s aunt said next confirmed it.

“Strangely, my brother calmed down after she threatened him. He spent the entire afternoon thinking, then agreed to her demand.” Fan Yu’s aunt wore a complicated expression. “Looking back, he was probably planning how to kill her, not considering the divorce.

“Everything went according to his plan. Rain was pouring down the day he locked Fan Yu in his office and returned home alone. When we realized Fan Yu was missing, we all went out to search for him. My brother led his wife to Mu Yang High School.

“When I came home at nine, none of them were there. I was worried, so I went to Mu Yang High School to look for them.

“There was an old well on the hill behind the school. Heavy rain had caused a landslide a few days earlier, burying it. When I arrived, my brother was clearing the earth from around the well.

“At first, I didn’t see my sister-in-law. I called my brother’s name as I approached. Then I saw her body wedged in the mouth of the well.

“I never thought he was capable of something like that. He was normally so gentle, and he truly loved his wife. That was when I realized he had lost his mind. I should have known the moment he brought home that photograph and said he was being haunted.

“After I stumbled upon the murder, he gave me two choices: help him hide the body or die.

“I wanted to live, so I obeyed. At his order, I made several wounds on my sister-in-law’s body, then helped him dig out the well.”

Fan Yu’s aunt leaned against the wall, regret filling her eyes. “I knew I had become his accomplice, but what frightened me more was not knowing when my brother would dispose of me. He would never leave a witness alive. Once he buried my sister-in-law, he might have thrown me into the well too.”

“So you killed him first?” From the woman’s account, Chen Ge concluded that the entire family had been deeply troubled. The husband was a voyeur, and rather than report him, his wife had used the secret as leverage to force a divorce.

“If I hadn’t killed him, he would have killed me. And once he was dead, I was Fan Yu’s only family. I never had to share him with anyone again.” That final sentence was probably the only honest thing she had said all night.

“But Fan Yu isn’t your child.” Chen Ge believed only half her story. The events had taken place three years ago, and no one remained to contradict her.

“You’re wrong! My children possessed Fan Yu’s body. That’s why he knows all their habits! Fan Yu isn’t just my brother’s child—he’s mine too!” Veins bulged across her face, and the force of her declaration split her lips.

Chen Ge decided not to press her further. She called her brother insane, but she was hardly stable herself. Her mind had probably broken when her husband and children died in the car accident. When she discovered that Fan Yu could see her children’s wandering spirits, she turned her distorted affection on him.

The distraught woman brought the black phone’s mission description to mind: everyone carries a deep well in their heart, where shameful, unknowable secrets lie buried.

“Get up. Show me the well where you dumped your brother’s body.”

“The well is gone. After my brother shoved my sister-in-law into it, I pushed him in after her. Her body broke his fall. He screamed and cursed from the bottom, but the rain was too heavy for anyone to hear.” Fan Yu’s aunt tugged nervously at her hair, her arms trembling. “I filled the well with earth. Three years have passed since then. I wouldn’t even know where to begin looking for it.”

“Just give me the general area,” Chen Ge said evenly, but the request provoked a violent reaction.

“No one will ever find them!” The memory cut into her, twisting her face with ferocity. “I’ll raise Fan Yu myself. I’ll give him all the love he needs!”

“If you truly loved Fan Yu, you wouldn’t have done this. Your love serves no one but you. It’s selfish.” At the Haunted House, Fan Yu had preferred speaking to a stranger over dealing with his own aunt. Their relationship was clearly fractured.

“You said the time after your family’s accident was the darkest period of your life. Fan Yu comforted you by bringing you drawings of your children. He reached out to you in kindness, and you killed his father.” Chen Ge thought of the small house filled with red figures. Had he not intervened, the situation might have taken a much darker, crueler turn. “You should be grateful Fan Yu is still a child.”

Facing the law would be best for both Fan Yu and his aunt. His search for heaven inside the well meant he had witnessed everything. He knew his aunt was the real killer.

As he grew older, he might have followed her example. Once he had blood on his hands, his life would have been ruined.

“It’s time to bring this tragedy to an end.” After stopping the livestream, Chen Ge had called the police. What punishment Fan Yu’s aunt might receive, he had no idea.

“That boy has been forced to live with his parents’ killer. No wonder his development has suffered. You’re the cause of his condition.”

At the mention of the police, Fan Yu’s aunt shook her head violently. Her lips moved soundlessly, and then she bolted toward the restroom door.

“Stop fighting this.” Chen Ge followed, afraid she might do something reckless.

The two raced down to the first floor. As they passed the sealed classroom, Fan Yu’s aunt suddenly tripped and lay sprawled on the ground. It looked as if something had yanked her leg.

Chen Ge stopped several meters behind her. She had fallen directly before the sealed classroom, a room that filled him with unease.

Pressing his back to the opposite wall, he leaned sideways to peer inside. It was after midnight. The supposedly empty classroom was full of students, and an old, rotund man stood at the lectern.
